headline: WhatsApp adds @all ping and anonymous polls to group chats
summary: The messaging app is rolling out new features to enhance group chat management, including an @all notification and improved poll options.
details: WhatsApp is introducing a new '@all' ping feature, similar to those found on Discord and Slack, to ensure all group members see important messages. This function is designed to alert everyone in a chat simultaneously, though its usage may vary depending on the group's dynamics.

To prevent overuse, the '@all' ping will be restricted to admins in group chats with over 32 participants. While these pings will bypass individual chat mutes, users can opt out of receiving '@all' notifications in their settings.

The messaging service is also revamping its polls feature. Users can now set an end time for voting and choose to conduct polls anonymously. Poll creators will have a 15-minute window to edit their questions after posting.

Additionally, WhatsApp is making it easier to start new conversations from existing groups. A new feature allows users to quickly split off into a separate chat with a subset of group members, streamlining side discussions.
